title: RFC 6455 protocol ownership
summary: The WebSocket layer owns RFC 6455 mechanics above an already-selected/accepted stream: Upgrade validation, directional framing and masking, fragmentation, message/control opcodes, ping/pong and close lifecycle. HTTP/TLS carrier ownership remains outside it.
invariants: Client frames are masked; server frames are unmasked.
Server access rejects unmasked client frames and reserved/RSV/control-frame violations fail closed.
Text, binary, continuation, ping, pong and close opcode identity is represented explicitly.
Extended payload lengths belong to WebSocketCodec, not to the carrier.
Fragmented TEXT/BINARY messages are reassembled while control frames may interleave.
Client and server handshake readers preserve post-header bytes so a coalesced first WebSocket frame is not discarded.
Server Upgrade admission supports expected path, Origin allowlist, subprotocol selection, version 13 and canonical key shape.
Ping/pong and close are WebSocket lifecycle; TCP/TLS shutdown remains owned by the stream provider/HTTPS wrapper.
permessage-deflate and other WebSocket extensions remain unimplemented.
RFC 8441 over HTTP/2 and RFC 9220 over HTTP/3 remain separate future carrier compositions.
